newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.3001 on Friday against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market from Thursday's 8.3008 due to short-covering, dealers said.
Traders said strong buying at about 8.3010 supported the yuan but was not enough to push it above 8.3000 at the close.
The yuan opened up at 8.3000 and consolidated in a narrow range of 8.3000 and 8.3005 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.3007 and high of 8.2990 in late trading.
Trading was less active than on Thursday, with most done at 8.3003, traders said.
One dealer said that there had been no negative news for the yuan. "Short-covering buying emerged in the market to push the yuan near 8.30," he said.

A second dealer said that the central bank was happy to see the yuan at the 8.30 level. "Its activity was limited to stop the yuan rising above 8.30 rather than depress it further," he said. Dealers expect the currency to continue moving around the key level of 8.3000 early next week.
The yuan closed up at an intraday high of 7.4300 from 7.4480 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at 1.0739 against the Hong Kong dollar.
